title: Nüwa: Mending the Spatial Integrity Torn by VLM Token Pruning
claim: Our pruned model retains most of the full model's accuracy across many benchmarks, beating prior pruning methods, especially on spatially sensitive tasks.
layout: 2 side-by-side radar charts, left-to-right, legends with retained-performance percentages
description: Two radar (spider) charts sit side by side. Panel (a) plots 10 VQA benchmarks (GQA, MMB, MMMU, MME, VQAv2, VQAtext, POPE, SQA, SEED, MMVet) on spokes. Panel (b) plots 3 visual grounding benchmarks, shown as 8 Refcoco-style spokes. Each method is a filled, smoothed polygon in its own color: purple for the vanilla unpruned model, green for Nüwa, blue for VisionZip, orange for SparseVLM and red for FastV. Numeric scores are printed along the spokes, and the vanilla maxima are in bold at the rim. Legends with colored badges give the percentage of vanilla performance retained, such as 94.8% and 93.9%. In panel (a) the polygons mostly overlap, so Nüwa is close to vanilla. In panel (b) the baselines collapse to tiny spikes at the center while the Nüwa variants (Nüwa-128 and Nüwa-64) stay large. A crown icon marks Nüwa.
caption: N\"uwa Performance On VQA and VG tasks, preserving 95% and 47% under 88.9% reduction of vision tokens. (a) Our N\"uwa outperforms current efficient VLMs on 10 VQA benchmarks; (b) On 3 visual grounding benchmarks, N\"uwa also achieves SOTA results.
abstract: Vision token pruning has proven to be an effective acceleration technique for the efficient Vision Language Model (VLM). However, existing pruning methods demonstrate excellent performance preservation in visual question answering (VQA) and suffer substantial degradation on visual grounding (VG) tasks. Our analysis of the VLM's processing pipeline reveals that strategies utilizing global semantic similarity and attention scores lose the global spatial reference frame, which is derived from the interactions of tokens' positional information. Motivated by these findings, we propose $\text{NÃ¼wa}$, a two-stage token pruning framework that enables efficient feature aggregation while maintaining spatial integrity. In the first stage, after the vision encoder, we apply three operations, namely separation, alignment, and aggregation, which are inspired by swarm intelligence algorithms to retain information-rich global spatial anchors. In the second stage, within the LLM, we perform text-guided pruning to retain task-relevant visual tokens. Extensive experiments demonstrate that $\text{NÃ¼wa}$ achieves SOTA performance on multiple VQA benchmarks (from 94% to 95%) and yields substantial improvements on visual grounding tasks (from 7% to 47%).
